title: Does Sex Help a Hangover? What It Can and Can't Fix
excerpt: Does sex help a hangover? What endorphins and oxytocin can and can't do for headache, mood, and sleep, when hangover sex makes things worse, and what actually helps.
metaDescription: Does sex help a hangover? How endorphins ease pain and mood, why it can worsen a headache or nausea, and what actually helps you recover.
author: DHM Guide Team
content:
**The honest answer first:** sex can make a hangover feel a bit better for a while, but it doesn't treat the hangover. Orgasm and physical closeness release feel-good chemicals (endorphins and oxytocin) that can dull pain a little, lift your mood, and help you relax or drift back to sleep. What sex can't do is rehydrate you, settle an irritated stomach, or help your body clear the leftovers of a night of drinking any faster. So if you feel up to it, go ahead and enjoy it. Just don't expect it to fix anything that water, food, and sleep would otherwise fix.

**The quick rules:** drink a big glass of water first. Take it easy if your head is pounding or your stomach is shaky. Stop if your headache gets sharply worse. Make sure you're both sober enough to clearly agree to it. If you used a condom or the pill the night before and something went wrong (a forgotten condom, or vomiting soon after taking your pill), deal with that today, not next week.

> **When to see a doctor or get help.** A normal hangover fades within a day. Get emergency care (call 911 in the US) if you have a **sudden, severe headache that peaks within seconds or a minute**, especially during or right after sex, a headache with a stiff neck, confusion, weakness, or trouble speaking, chest pain or a racing heartbeat that doesn't settle with rest, fainting, or vomiting you can't stop. See a doctor soon if headaches during sex keep happening, if you get erection problems often even when you haven't been drinking, or if you think you may need emergency contraception or STI testing. If you're shaking, sweating, or anxious every morning until you have a drink, that's a sign your body has come to depend on alcohol. It deserves a straightforward conversation with a doctor, because stopping suddenly can be risky.

## Does Sex Actually Help a Hangover? What's Going On in Your Body

To see why sex sometimes feels like it helps, it's worth looking at what a hangover actually is. It isn't one thing. It's a bundle of problems that arrive together the morning after drinking:

- **Poor sleep.** Alcohol helps you fall asleep but breaks up your sleep in the second half of the night, so you wake up tired even after eight hours in bed.
- **Fluid loss.** Alcohol makes you urinate more, so many people wake up mildly dehydrated, with a dry mouth and a headache.
- **Inflammation.** Heavy drinking triggers an immune response, which is part of why you feel achy, foggy, and generally unwell, almost like the start of a cold.
- **Stomach irritation.** Alcohol irritates the stomach lining and increases acid, which brings nausea and heartburn.
- **Breakdown products.** Your liver turns alcohol into acetaldehyde, a toxic compound, before turning it into something harmless. Some researchers think acetaldehyde and related compounds contribute to hangover misery.
- **Low mood and anxiety.** The brain rebounds after alcohol's calming effect wears off, which is why the next morning can feel jittery or flat ("hangxiety").

Now look at what sex does. During arousal and orgasm, your brain releases a mix of chemicals, including:

- **Endorphins**, the body's own painkillers, which can dull pain and give a sense of well-being.
- **Oxytocin**, sometimes called the bonding hormone, which is linked to feelings of closeness and calm.
- **Dopamine**, part of the brain's reward system, which drives that pleasant lift.
- **Prolactin**, which rises after orgasm and is thought to contribute to the relaxed, sleepy feeling afterwards.

Put the two lists side by side and the picture is clear. Sex can push back against the **pain** and the **mood** parts of a hangover, and it can help you get back to **sleep**, which is genuinely useful. It does nothing for fluid loss, inflammation, stomach irritation, or alcohol breakdown. That's why some people swear by it and others feel worse: it depends on which part of the hangover is bothering you most.

## The Headache Question: Can Sex Relieve or Worsen a Hangover Headache?

This is where the idea has the most real support, and also where it can backfire.

### The case for relief

There is research on sex and headaches, though not specifically hangover headaches. A study from the University of Münster in Germany, published in the journal *Cephalalgia* in 2013, surveyed people with migraine and cluster headache about sexual activity during an attack. A large share of the migraine patients who had sex during an attack reported that their pain improved, some of them completely. The researchers suggested endorphins released during orgasm might be acting as a natural pain reliever.

Separate lab research by Barry Komisaruk and Beverly Whipple at Rutgers found that genital stimulation raised pain thresholds in women, meaning they became less sensitive to painful stimuli during stimulation and orgasm.

So there is a reasonable basis for the idea that sex can take the edge off pain. Two caveats matter, though. First, the migraine study was a survey of people who chose to have sex during attacks, so it can't tell us how well it works for everyone. Second, a migraine is not a hangover headache. A hangover headache has different triggers, such as dehydration, poor sleep, and inflammation, which an orgasm doesn't touch.

### The case against

The same Münster survey found that a minority of patients said sex made their headache worse. That fits with what most people would expect. Sex is physical exertion. It raises your heart rate and blood pressure, and if your head is already throbbing, that extra pressure can make it pound harder.

There's also a recognized medical condition called **headache associated with sexual activity** (sometimes called coital or orgasmic headache). It can come on as a dull ache that builds with arousal, or as a sudden, explosive pain at or just before orgasm. Most cases are harmless, but a sudden, severe headache can also be a warning sign of bleeding in the brain. Because the two can feel similar, doctors treat a first-time thunderclap headache during sex as an emergency until it's been checked.

**In practice:** if your hangover headache is a dull, low-level ache, sex might help it fade for a bit. If it's already pounding, expect exertion to make it worse. And if a headache comes on suddenly and severely during sex, stop and get emergency care. For headache-specific fixes that actually work on the cause, see our guide to [hangover headache relief](/never-hungover/hangover-headache-fast-relief-methods-2025).

## Hangover Sex and Mood: Why It Can Feel So Good

A lot of what makes a hangover miserable isn't physical at all. It's the low, anxious, slightly guilty feeling that comes after a big night. Alcohol boosts calming brain chemistry while you drink, and when it wears off, your brain swings the other way. That rebound is a big part of why people feel on edge, irritable, or flat the next morning.

This is the part of a hangover where sex probably does the most good. The dopamine lift, the endorphins, and the closeness that comes with oxytocin can all counter that low mood, at least for an hour or two. Physical affection on its own, even without sex, can have a calming effect. If what's really bothering you is "hangxiety," a slow morning in bed with someone you trust may genuinely help you feel more like yourself.

It won't last forever. Once the glow fades, the underlying hangover is still there if you haven't dealt with the fluid loss and the lack of sleep. But feeling better for a while, then dozing off, is a decent outcome on a rough morning. If anxiety is your main hangover symptom, our [hangxiety guide](/never-hungover/hangxiety-complete-guide-2026-supplements-research) goes through what helps.

## Can Sex Help You Sleep Off a Hangover?

Yes, and this might be its most underrated benefit. Many people find they feel drowsy and relaxed after orgasm. The rise in prolactin and the general release of tension are thought to be part of that. On a hangover morning, that's useful, because one of the main reasons you feel awful is that alcohol broke up your sleep.

Alcohol tends to knock you out quickly, but as your body processes it during the night, your sleep becomes lighter and more broken, and you lose some of the restorative dream sleep (REM) you'd normally get. You wake up early, can't settle, and feel wrecked. If sex helps you fall back asleep for another hour or two, that extra rest will probably do more for your hangover than the sex itself.

For more on why rest helps and how to get it, see [does sleep help a hangover](/never-hungover/does-sleep-help-a-hangover).

## Can Sex Make a Hangover Worse?

It can, in a few predictable ways:

- **Dehydration gets worse.** You're already short on fluids. Sweating during sex adds to that. Drink a glass of water before and after.
- **Nausea.** Movement, especially lying flat or changing positions a lot, can unsettle an already shaky stomach. If you feel queasy, slow down or stop.
- **Headache.** As covered above, exertion can make a throbbing head throb harder.
- **Racing heart.** Alcohol can leave your heart rate a bit higher the next day, and exertion pushes it up further. A fast heartbeat that settles when you rest is usually fine. One that doesn't, or comes with chest pain or dizziness, is not. Our guide to [heart racing after drinking](/never-hungover/heart-racing-after-drinking) explains when to worry.
- **Low blood sugar.** Drinking can lower blood sugar, especially if you didn't eat much. Exertion on an empty stomach can leave you shaky or lightheaded. Eat something first if you can.

None of these are reasons to avoid sex entirely. They're reasons to listen to your body and treat it like light exercise: fine if you feel okay, not something to push through if you don't.

## Is Hangover Sex Like Exercise for a Hangover?

Sex is moderate physical activity, so the question overlaps with whether exercise helps a hangover. The answer is similar for both. Gentle movement can lift your mood, and some people find it shakes off the sluggishness. But exercise doesn't "sweat out" alcohol. Only a tiny fraction of alcohol leaves through sweat and breath, and your liver does almost all of the work at its own steady pace. Hard exertion while you're dehydrated can make you feel worse.

So if you think of hangover sex as a way to sweat out the toxins, that's not how it works. If you think of it as a pleasant, gentle activity that might boost your mood and help you sleep, that's about right. Our article on [whether exercise helps a hangover](/never-hungover/does-exercise-help-a-hangover) covers the same logic in more detail.

## Why Am I So Horny When I'm Hungover?

Plenty of people notice they feel more interested in sex when they're hungover, and it can seem strange when the rest of your body feels terrible. There isn't a definitive scientific explanation, but a few factors probably play a part:

- **Craving comfort.** After the crash that follows drinking, your brain is looking for something that feels good. Sex offers a reliable dopamine and endorphin lift.
- **Morning timing.** For many people, especially men, arousal and testosterone are naturally higher in the morning. Hangovers usually happen in the morning.
- **Opportunity.** You're often in bed with nowhere to be, sometimes with a partner who's in the same state.
- **Lowered inhibitions.** If you drank late, there may still be some alcohol in your system, which lowers inhibitions.

Some small lab studies have looked at whether alcohol changes sex hormones in the short term, with mixed and inconsistent results. It's unlikely to be the main reason. More likely, it's the combination of a brain looking for relief and a relaxed morning with time to kill.

For the bigger picture on how drinking affects desire, see our guide to [alcohol and libido](/never-hungover/alcohol-and-libido).

## Erection Problems and Arousal Issues the Morning After

The flip side is that a hangover can make sex harder to actually do. Alcohol is a depressant. It slows the nerve signals and affects the blood flow that arousal relies on. If you drank heavily or late, there can still be meaningful alcohol in your blood the next morning, because the body only clears roughly one standard drink per hour, and that varies from person to person.

The result can be difficulty getting or keeping an erection, reduced lubrication, or simply finding it harder to reach orgasm. Dehydration, fatigue, and feeling rough all add to it. This is very common, it's temporary, and it's not a sign that anything is wrong. Usually it resolves once you've slept, rehydrated, and the alcohol has cleared.

What's worth paying attention to is a pattern. If erection problems keep happening even on days when you haven't been drinking, that's worth raising with a doctor, since it can sometimes be an early sign of issues with blood vessels or blood sugar.

## Consent, Safety, and the Morning-After Checklist

A hangover morning comes with a few practical things to think about that are easy to brush past.

### Make sure you're both sober enough

Consent has to be clear and given by someone who understands what they're agreeing to. If either of you is still noticeably drunk, foggy, or confused in the morning, the right move is to wait. This matters just as much the morning after as it does the night before. A hangover alone doesn't stop someone from consenting, but still being drunk can.

### Check what happened with protection last night

Alcohol makes it far more likely that a condom gets forgotten, slips, or breaks, or that someone forgets a pill. If something went wrong:

- **Emergency contraception** works best the sooner it's taken. Some types are available from pharmacies without a prescription in many countries. A pharmacist can tell you which option fits your situation and how long you have.
- **STI testing** is worth thinking about if you had sex without a condom with a new partner. A clinic or doctor can tell you when testing is most accurate, since some infections take time to show up on tests.

### Vomiting and the birth control pill

If you vomited within a few hours of taking your pill, it may not have been fully absorbed. Many pill leaflets and health services advise treating this like a missed pill. Check the instructions for your specific brand or ask a pharmacist, and use condoms until you know you're protected.

### Painkillers and alcohol

If you take something for the headache before or after, keep in mind how common painkillers interact with alcohol. Ibuprofen and aspirin can irritate a stomach that alcohol has already upset, and acetaminophen (Tylenol) adds work for the liver. A single standard dose taken with food is usually fine for a healthy adult who doesn't drink heavily every day, but read the label. Our guide to [ibuprofen and alcohol](/never-hungover/ibuprofen-and-alcohol) has the details.

## What Actually Helps a Hangover (Before or After Sex)

If you want to feel properly better, these are the basics that do the heavy lifting. Sex is fine to add on top.

1. **Water first, with some electrolytes.** A glass or two of water, plus a drink or snack with some salt and potassium, helps with the dry mouth, headache, and lightheadedness. See [how to rehydrate after drinking](/never-hungover/how-to-rehydrate-after-drinking).
2. **Eat something bland.** Toast, eggs, bananas, rice, or crackers help steady blood sugar and give your stomach something easy to handle.
3. **More sleep.** If you can get back to sleep (with or without sex helping), take it. Rest is one of the few things that reliably helps.
4. **A pain reliever if you need one.** One standard dose with food, following the label and the alcohol warnings on it.
5. **Skip the hair of the dog.** Drinking more alcohol only postpones the hangover and adds to the strain on your body.
6. **Give it time.** Most hangovers fade within a day. Nothing, sex included, makes your body clear alcohol by-products much faster.

## Heading Off the Next Hangover

The best way to enjoy a lazy morning in bed is to not feel wrecked in the first place. The things that make the biggest difference are the least exciting:

- **Drink less, and slower.** Pace yourself to roughly one drink an hour and alternate with water.
- **Eat before and while drinking.** Food in your stomach slows how fast alcohol reaches your blood.
- **Choose lighter drinks.** Clear spirits tend to cause milder hangovers than dark ones like bourbon or red wine, though the amount you drink matters far more.
- **Stop earlier in the night.** Your body needs time to process alcohol before morning, and you'll sleep better.

Our full guide on [how to prevent a hangover](/never-hungover/how-to-prevent-a-hangover) goes through each of these in more depth.

Some people also add a supplement. **DHM (dihydromyricetin)** is a plant compound from the Japanese raisin tree that has been studied for its effects on how the body handles alcohol. Most of the research comes from animal and lab studies, with limited human data, so it's promising rather than proven. There is no good evidence that it prevents hangovers on its own, and it doesn't replace drinking less and staying hydrated. If you want to try it, a well-reviewed option is [No Days Wasted DHM Detox](https://www.amazon.com/dp/B0D4BWK6PH?tag=dhmguide-20), or a simple single-ingredient choice is [Double Wood Supplements DHM](https://www.amazon.com/dp/B074N712FM?tag=dhmguide-20). Our [DHM dosage guide](/never-hungover/dhm-dosage-guide-2025) covers how people typically take it. Check with a doctor or pharmacist first if you take prescription medicines.

## The Bottom Line

Sex won't cure a hangover, but it isn't a myth that it can help a little. The endorphins, oxytocin, and dopamine released during sex and orgasm can ease mild pain, lift a low or anxious mood, and help you get back to sleep, which is one of the few things that reliably helps. It does nothing for dehydration, a queasy stomach, or the inflammation behind that achy, foggy feeling, and exertion can make a pounding headache or nausea worse.

So drink some water first, go gently, stop if your head starts pounding harder, and make sure you're both sober enough to say yes. Then deal with the basics: fluids, food, rest, and time. And if a headache ever hits suddenly and severely during sex, treat it as an emergency.

## Frequently Asked Questions

**Does sex help a hangover?**

It can make you feel somewhat better for a while, but it doesn't treat the hangover itself. Orgasm and physical closeness release endorphins and oxytocin, which can ease pain a little, lift your mood, and help you relax or fall back asleep. None of that rehydrates you, settles your stomach, or speeds up how fast your body clears alcohol by-products. Think of it as a mood boost, not a cure.

**Can sex cure a hangover?**

No. There is no good evidence that sex cures a hangover or shortens it. A hangover is driven by poor sleep, dehydration, inflammation, stomach irritation, and the after-effects of alcohol breakdown. Sex doesn't fix any of those. It may take the edge off a headache or low mood for some people, which is why it feels like it helped.

**Can sex make a hangover worse?**

Sometimes. Exertion can make a pounding headache worse, sweating adds to fluid loss, and a sloshing stomach can tip into nausea. Some people also get a specific headache triggered by sexual activity. If sex makes your head pound harder, stop, drink water, and rest. A sudden, severe headache that hits like a thunderclap during or right after sex needs emergency care.

**Why am I so horny when I'm hungover?**

Nobody has a definitive answer, but a few things probably play a part. Your body is craving comfort and a dopamine lift after the crash that follows drinking, you may be in bed with a partner with nowhere to be, and morning is already a time when many people feel more aroused. Some lab research suggests alcohol can shift sex hormones in the short term, but the effects are small and inconsistent, so it's unlikely to be the main reason.

**Why can't I get or keep an erection when hungover?**

Alcohol can still be in your system the next morning if you drank late or heavily, and it dampens the nerve signals and blood flow that erections depend on. Dehydration, poor sleep, and feeling rough add to it. It's common, it's temporary, and it usually resolves once you've slept, rehydrated, and the alcohol has cleared. If it happens often when you haven't been drinking, it's worth raising with a doctor.

**Is it safe to have sex if I might still be drunk?**

Both of you need to be clearly able to consent, and that means sober enough to understand and agree to what's happening. If either of you is still noticeably drunk in the morning, wait. Being still drunk also makes forgetting condoms or contraception more likely, and alcohol in your blood can affect balance, judgment, and erections.

**Does vomiting from a hangover affect the birth control pill?**

It can. Many pill leaflets and health services advise that if you vomit within a few hours of taking a combined or progestogen-only pill, it may not have been absorbed and you should follow the missed-pill instructions for your brand. Check your pill's leaflet or ask a pharmacist, and use condoms until you're sure you're protected.

**Is sex better than other hangover remedies?**

It's pleasant, but it ranks below the basics. Water with some electrolytes, a bland meal, more sleep, and a standard dose of a pain reliever if you need one do more for the actual symptoms. Sex is fine to add on top if you feel up to it. For preventing the next hangover, drinking less, pacing yourself, and eating beforehand matter far more.
